skill.name: backend-development-feature-development
skill.description: Orchestrate end-to-end backend feature development from requirements to deployment. Use when coordinating multi-phase feature delivery across teams and services.
skill.summary: Coordinate backend feature delivery from requirements through implementation, testing, rollout, and monitoring.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The only static finding is a false positive. The flagged line is a safety instruction requiring approvals and rollback plans before production changes, not system reconnaissance or malicious behavior. No evidence found for prompt injection, data exfiltration, credential access, or unsafe command execution in SKILL.md.

static_findings.snippet: - Avoid production changes without approvals and rollback plans.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 32 tells users to avoid production changes without approvals and rollback plans. This is defensive operational guidance and does not request reconnaissance, credential access, or command execution.

content.value_statement: Complex backend features often fail when requirements, design, testing, and rollout are handled separately. This skill provides a phased workflow for coordinated delivery from discovery through deployment.
actual_capabilities: Defines a phased workflow from discovery through production rollout.
Supports traditional, TDD, BDD, and DDD development approaches.
Coordinates requirements, architecture, implementation, testing, security, and deployment tasks.
Includes rollout options such as canary, feature flags, blue-green deployment, and A/B testing.
Specifies expected outputs for each development phase.
limitations: Does not provide executable automation or generated application code by itself.
Assumes the needed specialist agents or equivalent expertise are available.
Best suited to multi-phase features, not small isolated bug fixes.
Requires user-provided product, architecture, deployment, and compliance context.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Backend Feature
use_cases.description: Create a structured plan for requirements, architecture, implementation, testing, rollout, and monitoring.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Cross-Team Delivery
use_cases.description: Align backend, frontend, data, security, and deployment work across a shared feature roadmap.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Controlled Release
use_cases.description: Define feature flags, deployment strategy, observability, rollback steps, and documentation before launch.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Medium Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan a medium backend feature for account-level usage quotas. Include requirements, architecture, testing, and rollout outputs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a normal feature delivery.

prompt_templates.title: Run a TDD Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the TDD methodology for a backend billing reminder feature. Define acceptance criteria, test phases, implementation steps, and release checks.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate a Multi-Service Rollout
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a complex feature that changes the user service, notification service, and analytics pipeline. Use feature flags and staged rollout controls.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Epic Release Program
prompt_templates.prompt: Orchestrate an epic backend platform migration with DDD, security validation, performance budgets, observability, rollback planning, and knowledge transfer.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert workflow for a major architectural change.

output_examples.input: Plan account-level usage quotas for an API product.
output: A requirements summary with user stories, success metrics, risks, and stakeholders.
A technical plan covering service boundaries, API contracts, data models, and rollout controls.
A delivery checklist for tests, security validation, monitoring, documentation, and rollback.

output_examples.input: Prepare a canary release for a notification service change.
output: A staged deployment plan with initial traffic percentage, health metrics, and rollback triggers.
A monitoring plan for latency, error rates, delivery success, and business impact.
A documentation plan for runbooks, release notes, and support handoff.

output_examples.input: Coordinate frontend, backend, and analytics work for a subscription feature.
output: A cross-team task sequence that links product requirements to implementation and validation.
Expected outputs for frontend integration, backend APIs, data events, and quality gates.
A release readiness view covering feature flags, coverage targets, alerts, and approval steps.

best_practices: Start with clear feature scope, success metrics, constraints, and ownership.
Carry prior phase outputs into later prompts to preserve context and decisions.
Validate security, performance, rollout, rollback, and monitoring before production release.
anti_patterns: Using the full workflow for a small isolated fix.
Skipping approvals, staging validation, or rollback planning for production changes.
Treating generated plans as final without review by responsible engineering owners.

faq.question: What kind of work is this skill best for?
faq.answer: It is best for backend features that need planning, implementation, testing, deployment, and team coordination.

faq.question: Can this skill write the production code for me?
faq.answer: It guides the development workflow and specialist tasks, but it does not include executable code by itself.

faq.question: Does it support test-driven development?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes TDD as a methodology option and defines test suite expectations.

faq.question: Does it include deployment planning?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers direct, canary, feature-flag, blue-green, and A/B test deployment strategies.

faq.question: Is it useful for small bug fixes?
faq.answer: No. The skill states that small isolated changes usually do not need the full workflow.
